question.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (-3F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,i+2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,j-4z\,k.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-3F) & =-3∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(4z) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4 \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4 \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-3F) & =-3∇\cdot F \\  & =-3\cdot 2(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2) \\  & =6(2-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$
